subject: Post-demo recap: Observability, ops comparisons & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Turner <chloe.turner@acme.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Observability & Ops questions

Hi Chloe / Tom 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Recap (what we showed)
- Unified Console: per-route dashboards, request tracing, and token-level cost breakdowns.
- Runtime diff: how our serving/runtime selects kernels and handles KV cache to keep p99 latency low under production loads.
- Rollouts & fallbacks: model variants, routing policies, and canary behavior.

2) Key differentiators vs hyperscalers (high-level)
- Production-first telemetry: request-level trace IDs + token cost breakdowns surfaced out-of-the-box in the Console (vs instrumenting multiple services).
- Predictable reserved capacity (Dedicated) with SLAs if you need throughput guarantees.
- Cost controls: batching + cache recommendations that are workload-aware, not just static settings.

3) Asks / next steps
- POC benchmarking run: Redwood vs your current inference (we recommend: 1) steady-state throughput, 2) cold-start/first-token p90/p95, 3) KV-cache effectiveness with prefix reuse).
- I'll share the eval plan and a short PDF comparing Redwood <> hyperscalers.
- We'll also surface SOC2 artifacts and a sample of audit logs for your security team.

Attached: Redwood-vs-hyperscalers.pdf (high-level comparison).

Feel free to confirm the POC window you'd prefer; Rafael and Nikhil will propose the instrumentation/metrics to capture.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: Redwood-vs-hyperscalers.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)]

Marissa  thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifying Qs before we lock in the POC:

Hey Chloe  quick answers and what we can ship for the POC: 

- Dashboards/screenshots: attaching a few Console screenshots showing per-route latency histograms, trace waterfall, and token-cost UI.
- Tracing: Yes  we emit request IDs and optional OpenTelemetry spans that can be correlated with your Datadog traces; we can provide a small sidecar example to forward spans.
- SLO examples (Hosted/Dedicated): for 512-token gen on our Dedicated pools we commonly observe p50 ~ 80ms, p95 ~ 240ms, p99 ~ 420ms (will vary by model/instance type). Hosted is slightly higher but similar shape.

Suggested metrics to capture for the POC:
- end-to-end latency (client -> response finish) p50/p95/p99
- model-inference time vs queue time (to observe batching effects)
- tokens generated per request and token-level cost attribution (Console provides a CSV export)
- cache hit rate for prefix reuse

We can enable request-level trace IDs for your first test tomorrow and share the sample logs. Attaching: ops-dashboard-screenshots.png

 Rafael
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Observability & Ops questions

Hi Chloe  specific POC plan and test steps (high level). I'm pasting the quick checklist and adding links to the shared docs: 

POC window: Wed-Fri next week (3x business days)
Prep (Day 0)
- Redwood will provision a scoped API key and a Dedicated test slot (or Hosted test env if you prefer).
- We'll share the instrumentation snippet for OpenTelemetry and an example Datadog mapping.

Tests (Day 1-2)
1) Latency/throughput: run steady-state load at target QPS (we recommend ~10-20 RPS for 512-token baseline), capture p50/p95/p99.
2) Cache effectiveness: run workloads with varying prefix reuse to measure KV-cache hit rate.
3) Batching sensitivity: vary batch windows (5ms/15ms/50ms) and observe cost vs latency trade-offs.
4) Failover: simulate capacity constraint and verify automatic fallback to hosted/compatible model.

Deliverables (Day 3)
- CSV exports of per-request metrics + Console screenshots.
- Short write-up of recommended batching/cache config for your workload.

Docs / Links:
- Eval plan: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cExamplePOC
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-024

If this looks good I'll create the Drive folder with the specific test harness scripts (simple k6/locust jobs) and share credentials via the secure link.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
